title: Global Logistics Inventory Synchronization
business: A global logistics provider managing real-time inventory across thousands of regional warehouses.
problem: Legacy polling mechanisms create high latency and database contention, causing inventory discrepancies when multiple regional hubs update stock levels simultaneously.
solution: NATS provides a unified messaging backbone using Pub-Sub for real-time inventory broadcasts, Request-Reply for immediate stock verification, and JetStream for persistent, reliable event streaming of transaction logs.
steps: Deploy a NATS cluster to act as the central message broker for all regional warehouse nodes.
Implement Pub-Sub topics for broadcasting inventory updates to all interested regional dashboards.
Utilize Request-Reply patterns for synchronous stock checks between a warehouse and the central database.
Configure JetStream streams to persist critical transaction events, ensuring data recovery if a regional node disconnects.
Establish consumer groups within JetStream to process inventory reconciliation tasks in parallel.
outcome: The system achieves eventual consistency across global nodes with reduced database load and improved responsiveness for stock verification requests.
limitation: JetStream persistence introduces storage overhead and potential latency during stream replication; monitor consumer lag metrics to ensure the system keeps pace with incoming transaction volume.

It automatically encrypts all warehouse data at rest.
It eliminates the need for any network communication between hubs.
questions.explanation: The solution leverages NATS messaging patterns to replace inefficient polling with event-driven updates and direct requests.
questions.evidence: NATS provides a unified messaging backbone using Pub-Sub for real-time inventory broadcasts, Request-Reply for immediate stock verification, and JetStream for persistent, reliable event streaming of transaction logs.

questions.question: In Global Logistics Inventory Synchronization, what is the primary trade-off when using JetStream for persistence?
options: It requires a manual restart of the cluster every hour.
It forces all messages to be sent synchronously.
It introduces storage overhead and potential latency during stream replication.
It prevents the use of Pub-Sub topics entirely.
questions.explanation: Persistence in JetStream requires disk I/O and replication, which adds overhead compared to ephemeral core NATS messaging.
questions.evidence: JetStream persistence introduces storage overhead and potential latency during stream replication; monitor consumer lag metrics to ensure the system keeps pace with incoming transaction volume.
